Details review about some faculties (3)
[MKT465- ZTK, MKT202- Nym, ENG103- Sye, MGT368- SSH2, INB372- SSA1, ENV107L-- ASA2, HIS102-- Abs3]. 
MKT465- Ztk. 
The first thing is learning. Madam onek joss poray. Every topics onek joss poray. Brand management niye madam er onek idea ache. So, class lecture gula onek effective hoy. Madam class lecture er pashapashi onek case study poray. So, real market scenario somporkeo ekta valo idea hoy. 
The second thing is, exam pattern. Quiz MCQ. 3/4 to best 2 count korbe. Quiz er jonno, slide and class lecture valo kore note kore pore gelei enough. 
Mid and Final e written and mcq thake. Mcq quiz er motoi. Madam mcq te onek brand (maximum e unknown) example diye questions kore. So, topics somporke idea thaka must. Written er jonno, madam case  study dibe. Then oi basis e question korbe. Madam per question er por ekta box rakhe. Habi jabi jinish na likhe exact point e likhben. Mid and final e pencil, eraser, color pencil niye jaben. Because, madam exam e Brand logo, Brand Character, Ad eshob aakte bolbe. 
Now, the third thing is, Individual Presentation, Group report and Group presentation. Individual Presentation er topic khub e simple. If you are a product, tahole ki hoten? Seta ke kivabe apni brand banaben? Group report e ekta GI products assign koredibe madam prottekta group ke. Oitar upor group report and presentation dite hobe. Presentation slide e spelling mistake kora jabe na. Madam donot like this. 
Madam ektu strict and 19 to 20 hle bokaboki kore. So, madam er rules mene cholte hobe. 
Grading fair. Curve koren na generally.
MKT202- Nym. 
First of all, Ma’am teaches very well. She uses numerous brand examples while explaining every topic, which makes the concepts easier to understand.
Exams: There will be 4 quizzes, and the best 2 will be counted. Each quiz will have 5-mark MCQs. To do well in the quizzes, you must carefully listen to and take notes during class lectures, along with thoroughly following the book and slides. If you do this, securing good marks will be easy.
For the midterm and final exams, there will be both MCQs and written questions. Following the quiz preparation technique is enough for the MCQs. The written part has two types of questions: short questions (2–3 marks) and long, situation-based questions. For short questions, just write concise and accurate answers to get full marks. For the long questions, align your concept with the given situation and write accordingly to score well. Ma’am likes clear and organized answers, so be sure to maintain that.
Report and Presentation: Follow her guidelines properly while writing the report and try to include creative concepts. If possible, create a TVC (Television Commercial) ad, as it impresses her. During the presentation, she usually remains normal, but she will ask a few questions at the end.
Grading: Ma’am’s grading is fair. You will receive exactly what you deserve. 
ENG103- Sye.
Sye is a blessing. 
Teaching - excellent. 
You have to write a lot of essay in this course. Madam marks valoi dey. Class lecture follow korte hobe. 
Grading - Curve queen. Madam onek joss grading kore. Ja deserve koren, seta to paben e. 1/2 grade maximum time curve kore. 
And, Madam is a fan of Shahrukh khan. so, madam ke boilen amio Shahrukh khan fan and movie dekhi Shahrukh khan er. Madam onek khusi hoye jaabe.
MGT368- SSH2. 
Sir er lecture ektu boaring. He is a old man. So, kotha ektu aste aste bole. But he has a vast knowledge about the whole entrepreneurship. He donot follow any kind of slides in his class, so you have to follow the books. 
He will give you so much both individual and group assignments. You have to complete it timely and submit all. Besides, His question pattern is much easy. Just book ta valo kore porle and common sense use kore likhle valo marks pawa somvob. And, try to publish a journal in a renowned newspaper. Sir onek pochondo kore eta. And, you will get a bonus marks. The main thing is Viva. Sir written e sobaikei valo marks dey so, sir mainly ekta viva ney. Jeta diye uni judge kore mainly student. Viva perfectly dite try korben. Tahole A/A- confirm. Overall grading joss.
INB372-SSA1. 
Ssa1 is a good faculty, undoubtedly. He is not orthodox in terms of teaching and is easy to understand and learn from. 
His grading’s fairly lenient if you are focused and attentive in his classes. Interact with him on relevant topics too. Also, pick up a few global news insights here and there, helps in his classes. Definitely read the book, if you can give references from there during the mid and final, he will give you full marks. Do not miss his classes as he hates that and will only consider upto three classes missed. Try to take up the CR spot too.
ENV107L- ASA2. 
Sir poray valo. Sir er slide porle enough. Total 8 class lab e. 
1 quiz, 1 final, 6 lab report. Etai course structure.  
Quiz-- Slide vlo kore porte hobe. Slide er kichu kichu jayga sir red color diye underline kore. Oi line gula beshi important. Valo kore slide porle enough. 
Final-- Final er aage sir ekta suggestions dey. Suggestions theke porlei common pore jay. 
6 lab report -- Total 6 ta lab report ache. Lab kore class e dekhabe. Tarpor sir er instructions onujayi lab report likhe sir ke joma dite hobe. 
Grading --- Fairly. Basically Final and lab report is the main indicator of grading. Quiz e sobai valo marks pay. That's why.
HIS102 – Abs3
The teacher’s voice is a bit slow, but he teaches very well. First, let’s talk about the contents of HIS102. This course mainly covers ancient world civilizations and global transformations during the Middle Ages, such as the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution. Faculty Reviews: MBK1, AFI2
MBK1 Ma’am (Ms. Marzan Bintey Kamal) - HIS101, HIS102, HIS103
I took HIS101 under ma’am in Fall 25 and HIS103 under ma’am in Summer 26. I have not done HIS102 with her. However, as all three of these are 100-level history courses, my experience with the two courses I have done with her should be of assistance. Additionally, she has started teaching HIS102 very recently, so you won’t find many reviews about her particularly for this course. But the following review is entirely based on my experience of HIS101 and HIS103 under her.
History is a boring subject to most of us. However, the way ma’am conducts the classes makes the course content very lively and interesting. She is very student-friendly and has an exceptional command over the course content.
To make the lectures interesting and explain the content easily, she adds information outside of the slides as well. This makes the actual content easier to understand and remember it as a story instead of a history lecture. But not to worry, all the questions come from the slides. So it’s a win-win situation.
For the MCQ part, read the slides thoroughly. For the written part, the answers to the questions are also in the slides, so again, you don’t need to read anything outside of the slides. For the broad and short questions, ma’am usually gives suggestions and also tells how to answer those questions if they come in the exam. So again, attending all the lectures is crucial if you want to do well. The short and broad questions usually come from the suggestions. Even if they are not from the suggestions, they will surely be from the slides.
One tip to do well in the written part is to follow ma’am’s instructions for writing the specific answers. And do not make your answers too concise; provide enough relevant information in your answers. Do not be afraid; you don’t need to write a 10-page essay for a question. You answer according to the questions. Not all questions require the same length of answer. When you are aiming for a good grade and studying enough, you will realise that you have a decent amount to write.
I used to be very afraid of history courses because I used to think I would need to memorise many years/dates. But for both of the courses, ma’am requires us to remember only a few specific years/dates mentioned by her.
In both of the courses, there is no presentation or report or any other group task, but an individual assignment, quizzes, a mid, a final, and a viva. The worst quiz is dropped, as usual. There are three quizzes in HIS103, but sadly, I forgot the number of quizzes she took in HIS101. Most probably, there were three quizzes in HIS101 as well.
She curves, but even without her curving, getting the top grade is easily possible. But curving may also be affected by the overall performance of the class.
Now, time for some personal experiences. Based on my experience and that of several friends who took one course under ma’am and another under a different faculty member, I’d say Ma’am’s lectures and overall way of conducting the course are significantly better.
AFI2 Ma’am (Ms. Afsana Islam) - ENV107L
Ma’am is very sweet and easy-going. She is the course coordinator for ENV107 Lab.
The majority of the questions in the quiz and the final exam come from her lectures and slides. One or two questions that do not come directly from the slides are either based on common-sense or indirectly given from the slides. She additionally provides suggestions as well. One thing I truly love and respect about her is that she does not get irritated when asked the same question repeatedly, if necessary.
Ma’am gives marks quite fairly. You can see all of your assignments/reports/experiments and the quiz paper. The only script that you can’t see directly is the final’s.
Again, in the experiments, she gives marks quite fairly, and I’d say leniently as well. At the same time, your marks may get deducted a little due to simple or minor but genuine mistakes. So form your group wisely, as the experiments make up a significant portion of the total marks.
She usually curves, but the performance of the section might also be a factor. Lastly, for A and A-, curving may not be applied as well, again depending on the overall performance of the section.

BBA students must take any two courses from HIS101, HIS102, HIS103, or HIS205.
However, many students often get confused about the content of these courses—what each course covers, which one is interesting, which one might be boring, etc. So, I am providing a detailed discussion on all four courses: HIS101, HIS102, HIS103, and HIS205. Hopefully, this will help you.
HIS101 – The title of this course is "History and Culture of Bangladesh."
The content of this course can be divided into several parts:
Ancient Archaeology of Bengal – In this section, you'll learn in detail about ancient archaeological sites of Bengal, such as Mahasthangarh, Paharpur, Mainamati, and Wari-Bateshwar.
Ancient and Medieval History of Bengal – This section covers the history of various kings and rulers of ancient and medieval Bengal, different regimes, and the lifestyle of that time. The course generally covers up to the period before the Battle of Plassey.
Culture of Bengal – This includes various cultural topics like Sufism, how Sufism spread in Bengal, the arrival of Islam, and traditional folk music of Bengal such as Lalon Fakir's songs and Baul music, along with celebrations like Pohela Boishakh.
Modern Social Reformers of Bengal – You will learn about social reformers from both Islamic and Hindu backgrounds in Bengal, such as Raja Rammohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Syed Ahmed Ali, and others.
HIS103 – The title of this course is "Emergence of Bangladesh."
This course starts from the Battle of Plassey and covers the entire British colonial period and the era of Pakistan. You will study in detail various movements and wars during these times. The course concludes with the Liberation War of Bangladesh.
HIS102 – The title of this course is "Introduction to World Civilization."
Unlike HIS101 and HIS103, which include historical topics you might have studied during school, most of the content in HIS102 and HIS205 is likely to be new for many students.
In HIS102, you will first learn about ancient civilizations of the world. These include the Egyptian civilization, Mesopotamian civilization, Indus Valley civilization, Vedic period, Chinese civilization, Hebrew civilization, Persian civilization, Arab civilization, Greek civilization, Roman civilization, and the Mayan civilization. You’ll explore their histories, how these civilizations developed, and their contributions to the world.
The course then moves into early modern history, covering important topics like the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution. Additionally, you’ll learn about major world religions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, Confucianism, Islam, Zoroastrianism, Christianity, and Judaism.
HIS205 – The title of this course is "World History."
This course mainly focuses on modern world history. HIS205 essentially picks up where HIS102 ends. It begins with the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution and then moves on to topics such as the French Revolution, World War I and World War II, the division of Germany, the Cold War, and other significant global historical events of recent centuries.
So, this was an overview of the main content of all four courses. Now it's your decision—which two courses will you choose?

BBA students must take any two courses from HIS101, HIS102, HIS103, or HIS205.
However, many students often get confused about the content of these courses—what each course covers, which one is interesting, which one might be boring, etc. So, I am providing a detailed discussion on all four courses: HIS101, HIS102, HIS103, and HIS205. Hopefully, this will help you.
HIS101 – The title of this course is "History and Culture of Bangladesh."
The content of this course can be divided into several parts:
Ancient Archaeology of Bengal – In this section, you'll learn in detail about ancient archaeological sites of Bengal, such as Mahasthangarh, Paharpur, Mainamati, and Wari-Bateshwar.
Ancient and Medieval History of Bengal – This section covers the history of various kings and rulers of ancient and medieval Bengal, different regimes, and the lifestyle of that time. The course generally covers up to the period before the Battle of Plassey.
Culture of Bengal – This includes various cultural topics like Sufism, how Sufism spread in Bengal, the arrival of Islam, and traditional folk music of Bengal such as Lalon Fakir's songs and Baul music, along with celebrations like Pohela Boishakh.
Modern Social Reformers of Bengal – You will learn about social reformers from both Islamic and Hindu backgrounds in Bengal, such as Raja Rammohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Syed Ahmed Ali, and others.
HIS103 – The title of this course is "Emergence of Bangladesh."
This course starts from the Battle of Plassey and covers the entire British colonial period and the era of Pakistan. You will study in detail various movements and wars during these times. The course concludes with the Liberation War of Bangladesh.
HIS102 – The title of this course is "Introduction to World Civilization."
Unlike HIS101 and HIS103, which include historical topics you might have studied during school, most of the content in HIS102 and HIS205 is likely to be new for many students.
In HIS102, you will first learn about ancient civilizations of the world. These include the Egyptian civilization, Mesopotamian civilization, Indus Valley civilization, Vedic period, Chinese civilization, Hebrew civilization, Persian civilization, Arab civilization, Greek civilization, Roman civilization, and the Mayan civilization. You’ll explore their histories, how these civilizations developed, and their contributions to the world.
The course then moves into early modern history, covering important topics like the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution. Additionally, you’ll learn about major world religions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, Confucianism, Islam, Zoroastrianism, Christianity, and Judaism.
HIS205 – The title of this course is "World History."
This course mainly focuses on modern world history. HIS205 essentially picks up where HIS102 ends. It begins with the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution and then moves on to topics such as the French Revolution, World War I and World War II, the division of Germany, the Cold War, and other significant global historical events of recent centuries.
So, this was an overview of the main content of all four courses. Now it's your decision—which two courses will you choose?
